title: KV Economizer Advisor: hit-curve synthesis, TTL budgeting, and safe config gating
creator: Amina R. Patel
description: Purpose: build an automated advisor and safe-apply workflow that recommends KV/prefix cache key designs, TTL budgets, and batching adjustments per route/tenant. The advisor should synthesize a hit-curve (probability a prefix is re-used vs age), compute an economical TTL budget given token cost and latency SLOs, and produce a staged rollout plan with deterministic rollback triggers. This ticket drives the engineering work to prototype the advisor, wire it into the config registry, and provide a gated apply pipeline with shadow testing and automatic rollback conditions.
acceptance_criteria: Advisor produces per-route candidate cache key schemata and TTL ranges with estimated cost delta and hit-rate uplift
Offline simulator reproduces observed production hit-rate within ±10% for three sample tenants
Safe-apply pipeline staged canary: shadow roll (10%), monitored ramp to 50% and full apply with automated rollback triggers in CI/CD
Rollback triggers defined and enforced: hit-rate regression > 8% absolute or token-cost increase > 12% or p95 latency regression > 20ms
Documentation and runbook published with example queries and remediation steps
decisions: Modeling approach: use mixed Poisson+hazard model (empirical inter-arrival + exponential tail) to synthesize hit-curve instead of relying purely on LR/ML models — simpler to simulate and explain to SREs
TTL budgets computed as knapsack-style optimization: maximize cost reduction subject to SLO constraints and a configurable safety multiplier
Canary strategy: start with shadowing followed by traffic canary (10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with minimum dwell time of 30 minutes between steps
Gating: metric-based automatic rollback enforced by pipeline; manual abort available to oncall via console action link
tasks: Instrument prefix access traces into dedicated sampling topic (schema, sampling fraction) — Diego
Implement hit-curve synthesizer service (inputs: sample trace, prefix bucketing, TTL candidate grid) — 4d
Build offline simulator that accepts synthesized curves and replay weights to predict cost/hitrate/latency — 3d
Integrate advisor output into config-registry: produce proposed config JSON with metadata and safety thresholds — 2d
Implement safe-apply pipeline steps: shadowing harness, canary traffic shifter, metric checks, automated rollback hook — 5d
Create dashboards and alert rules for rollouts (SLO deltas, token-cost delta, hit-rate time series) — 2d
Write runbook and example remediation steps including how to back out specific prefix rules — 1d
testing_plan: Unit tests for hit-curve synthesizer (edge cases: sparse prefixes, bursty arrivals)
Integration tests: run simulator against historical windows covering holiday/burst traffic
Canary shadow tests on staging with synthetic workload generator (tenant emulation)
Chaos test: inject delayed responses to ensure rollback triggers fire on latency regression
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Read-only advisor rollout to console (no apply) — expose recommendations to PM/Design for review
Stage 1: Shadow apply to 0% traffic for three sentinel routes for 48h
Stage 2: Traffic canary 10% for 30m, observe metrics, if OK -> 25% for 30m -> 50% for 60m -> 100%
Stage 3: Post-apply monitoring window 24h with tightened alerts; automatic rollback window 72h where config changes are reversible via single action
Emergency: immediate global rollback if any auto-trigger condition met during canary
monitoring_queries: HIT_RATE(ts) = sum(prefix_hits) / sum(prefix_lookups) grouped by route, tenant
TOKEN_COST_DELTA = (cost_after - cost_before) / cost_before (calc using token_unit_price * tokens_served)
LATENCY_P95_DELTA = p95_after - p95_before (use per-route latencies via tracing index)
PRODUCTION_SHADOW_DISCREPANCY = compare(response_hashes_before, response_hashes_after) rate — flag >0.5% as functional drift
